messages:
emma: heads-up onboarding hydra-6b (converted from transformers weights) — after int8 quant + our rotary->pos-adapter, summarization BLEU and a couple of rerank metrics dropped vs fp16. quick bench: mistral-7b fp16 P@1=0.62, hydra fp16 P@1=0.60, hydra int8+adapter P@1=0.51 :grimacing:
li: annoying. do we know if tokenizer/vocab changed during conversion? sometimes merges/special tokens shift indices and that kills specific prompts.
noah: i diffed vocab.json vs our canonical tokenizer. hydra has two extra soft tokens added around emojis and a merged token for "©" which shifts indices after 50256. conversion script assumed contiguous vocab and remapped by index, not token string  that's likely the cause.
emma: good catch. examples show missing license/copyright mentions in outputs. see sample below.
emma: prompt: "List legal considerations for redistributing scraped forum posts."
emma: hydra fp16: "Consider copyright, contributor consents, PII, and third-party licenses. Redact PII, add provenance, and consult counsel."
emma: hydra int8+adapter: "Be careful about quality, privacy and license. Use filters." <-- terse and loses juridical terms
zara: could be two things interacting: vocab index shift + adapter mapping for rotary frequencies. If high-index tokens now map to different embeddings and adapter rescales positional slopes, the quantized model flattens logits for those tokens.
li: i inspected embedding matrix slice around the shifted region. fp16 embeddings for token id 50257 spike in L2 norm vs neighbors, but after int8 quant we clip to a smaller dynamic range, so rare high-norm tokens get squashed.
noah: suggestions: 1) remap tokens by string not by index during conversion; 2) preserve per-token L2 scale in quant calibration (per-embedding-row scaling). We can try per-row int8 for embedding table only.
emma: i'll re-run conversion with token-string remap and a calibration pass that records per-row absmax for embeddings. small script:
eemma: ```python
# convert_remap.py (sketch)
with open('vocab.json') as f: vocab = json.load(f)
new_ids = {tok: i for i, tok in enumerate(target_vocab)}
mapping = [new_ids.get(tok, unknown_id) for tok in source_vocab]
# write remapped state dict by token string
```
zara: for the adapter: current freqs resample code averages and then quantizes slopes globally. try computing headwise slopes from raw freqs and keep them fp32 before quantizing other params. also consider per-head fp16 stash for slopes in runtime.
li: i'm curious if hydra uses a sparser rotary schedule (freqs spaced log-ish). if so resampling to linear grid will alias and produce weaker long-range attention.
noah: confirmed: hydra.rotary.freqs is log-spaced. adapter linear resample produced aliasing. i'll patch adapter to detect monotonicity and preserve log spacing in slope computation.
ops-bot: [ci-run] hydra/int8-remap+per-row-embed-calib queued (job 1769999991). logs at /ci/jobs/1769999991
emma: ran a 40-prompt smoke locally with remapped vocab + per-row embed quant -> P@1 int8 = 0.575 (was 0.51). big win. still ~0.025 from fp16.
zara: that residual gap could be from attention head scaling quantization. try per-head symmetric quant for Q/K/V and per-head bias compensation during calibration.
li: also check tokenizer special-casing of newline and sentinel tokens; sometimes string-remap misses internal tokenizers that post-process unknown tokens differently.
noah: i'll push a bench run with per-head QKV quant and keep rotary slopes fp32. running job 1769999992.
ops-bot: [ci-run] hydra/per-head-qkv queued (job 1769999992). ETA ~20m :hourglass_flowing_sand:
emma: thanks team. plan: 1) upstream conversion fix (string remap) 2) adapter change to preserve log-freq mapping + headwise slopes 3) embedding per-row quantization for rare/high-norm tokens 4) run full eval and decide if we need a fallback fp16 path for position slopes in Dedicated. filing a short RFC for the runtime fallback behavior. :thumbsup:
